arxiv-2210-14719.title: The appearance function for paper-folding words
arxiv-2210-14719.creator: Rob Burns
arxiv-2210-14719.description: Abstract We provide a complete characterisation of the appearance function for paper-folding sequences for factors of any length. We make use of the software package Walnut to establish these results. 1 Introduction The regular paper-folding sequence begins 1, 1, -1, 1, 1, -1, -1, 1, … .

arxiv-2211-16024.title: MmWave Mapping and SLAM for 5G and Beyond
arxiv-2211-16024.creator: Yu Ge, Ossi Kaltiokallio, Hyowon Kim, Jukka Talvitie, Sunwoo Kim, Lennart Svensson, Mikko Valkama, Henk Wymeersch
arxiv-2211-16024.description: Abstract Device localization and radar-like mapping are at the heart of integrated sensing and communication, enabling not only new services and applications, but can also improve communication quality with reduced overheads. These forms of sensing are however susceptible to data association problems, due to the unknown relation between measurements and detected objects or targets.

arxiv-2304-02725.title: FMG-Net and W-Net: Multigrid Inspired Deep Learning Architectures For Medical Imaging Segmentation
arxiv-2304-02725.creator: Adrian Celaya, Beatrice Riviere, David Fuentes
arxiv-2304-02725.description: Abstract Accurate medical imaging segmentation is critical for precise and effective medical interventions. However, despite the success of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in medical image segmentation, they still face challenges in handling fine-scale features and variations in image scales. These challenges are particularly evident in complex and challenging segmentation tasks, such as the BraTS multi-label brain tumor segmentation challenge.

arxiv-2408-08063.title: Constraining Ultralight ALP Dark Matter in Light of Cosmic Birefringence
arxiv-2408-08063.creator: Dongdong Zhang, Elisa G. M. Ferreira, Ippei Obata, Toshiya Namikawa
arxiv-2408-08063.description: Abstract Cosmic birefringence, the observed rotation of the polarization plane of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), serves as a compelling probe for parity-violating physics beyond the Standard Model. This study explores the potential of ultralight axion-like particle (ALP) dark matter to explain the observed cosmic birefringence in the CMB.

arxiv-2503-15926.title: Modeling Face Emotion Perception from Naturalistic Face Viewing: Insights from Fixational Events and Gaze Strategies
arxiv-2503-15926.creator: Meisam J. Seikavandi a , Maria J. Barrett b , and Paolo Burelli a
arxiv-2503-15926.description: Abstract Face Emotion Recognition (FER) is essential for social interactions and understanding others’ mental states. Utilizing eye tracking to investigate FER has yielded insights into cognitive processes. In this study, we utilized an instructionless paradigm to collect eye movement data from 21 participants, examining two FER processes: free viewing and grounded FER.

arxiv-2505-19890.title: Hurwitz-Brill-Noether theory via K ​ 3 K3 surfaces and stability conditions
arxiv-2505-19890.creator: Gavril Farkas, Soheyla Feyzbakhsh, Andrés Rojas
arxiv-2505-19890.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gavril Farkas, Soheyla Feyzbakhsh, Andrés Rojas. We develop a novel approach to the Brill–Noether theory of curves endowed with a degree k k cover of 𝐏 1 \mathbf{P}^{1} via Bridgeland stability conditions on elliptic K ​ 3 K3 surfaces. We first develop the Brill–Noether theory on elliptic K ​ 3 K3 surfaces via the notion of Bridgeland stability type for objects in their derived category.

pmc-12285468.description: omputed tomography)을 시행하였다. 경부 전산화 단층 촬영에서 왼쪽(level IV)에 4.3×2.8 cm 크기의 경부 식도 게실이 관찰되었다. 경부식도게실에 의해 갑상선(thyroid gland)의 좌측엽(left lobe)이 전방치환(anterior displacement)되어 있고, 또한 인접한 연조직(soft tissue)들도 경도로 전방치환(mild anterior displacement)이 있었다. 따라서 이로 인해 왼쪽 경부 부종(left neck swelling)을 호소할 가능성이 있었다(Fig. 1). 환자는 소화기내과로 의뢰되었고 외래를 방문하였다.

pmc-12437724.title: Recommendations for digital phenotyping using consumer grade wearable devices among people with severe mental illness: lessons from a systematic review of the literature
pmc-12437724.creator: L. Hassan, C. Sawyer, A. Milton, J. Torous, A. J. Casson, A. Davies, B. Ruiz-Yu, J. Firth
pmc-12437724.description: IntroductionDigital wearable devices, such as smartphones and smartwatches, have shown potential for passively monitoring mental and physical health in individuals with Severe Mental Illness (SMI), such as schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. While research-grade devices are well studied, consumer-grade wearables could offer a more accessible alternative, though their utility in this specific context remains underexplored.

pmc-12733053.title: Prenatal Identification of an EDA Variant in Dichorionic Male Twins: CfDNA Signal with Invasive Confirmation
pmc-12733053.creator: Simone Marcella, Roberto Sirica, Nadia Petrillo, Monica Ianniello, Alessio Mori, Rosa Castiello, Sossio Federico Capone, Eloisa Evangelista, Teresa Suero, Raffaella Ruggiero, Alfredo Columbro, Antonio Barone, Ioannis Malandrenis, Antonio Fico, Giovanni Savarese, Darren Griffin
pmc-12733053.description: Background/Objectives: X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia (XLHED) is a rare monogenic disorder characterized by hypohidrosis, hypotrichosis, and hypodontia, caused primarily by pathogenic variants in the EDA gene. XLHED predominantly affects males due to its X-linked recessive inheritance, while female carriers may exhibit variable phenotypes due to random X-inactivation. Early diagnosis is critical for timely counseling and emerging therapeutic interventions.

pmc-13067070.title: Learning to navigate interprofessional boundaries in health care
pmc-13067070.creator: Julia Paxino, Christy Noble, Walter Eppich
pmc-13067070.description: Health professionals must navigate complex systems—and that means negotiating role boundaries. Making this “boundary work” explicit in HPE can strengthen collaboration, clarity, and patient care. #HealthProfessionsEd #InterprofessionalEducation In health care, professional roles are becoming increasingly challenging to navigate. More clinical complexity demands specialisation, while workforce shortages require role diversification.

pmc-13334783.title: PREOPERATIVE PHYSIOTHERAPY AND ONE-YEAR PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES AFTER PRIMARY TOTAL KNEE ARTHROPLASTY: A REGISTRY-BASED COHORT STUDY OF 1,688 PATIENTS
pmc-13334783.creator: Siri B WINTHER, Mani IZADI, Vigdis K S HUSBY, Otto S HUSBY, Mathias F BROBAKKEN, Frank-David ØHRN, Jomar KLAKSVIK, Eivind WANG, Ole Kristian BERG
pmc-13334783.description: ObjectivePreoperative physiotherapy in patients receiving primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) aims to relieve pain, delay surgery, and improve postoperative recovery. This study investigates the change in PROMs and pain after primary TKA between patients who received preoperative physiotherapy (P) and those who did not (NP).DesignRegistry-based cohort study with data from an institutional registry.

pmc-13574644.title: From spatial intervention to healthy ageing: proposing a Spatial–Social–Ecological framework for active ageing community renewal
pmc-13574644.creator: Min Zhou, Yang Li, Jing Huang, Simeng Liu
pmc-13574644.description: IntroductionCommunity renewal oriented toward active ageing has become an important strategy for addressing population ageing and urban regeneration. However, existing research often examines spatial, social and ecological factors separately, resulting in a limited understanding of how community renewal can promote sustainable health outcomes.
